nancystanislas.name: Place Stanislas
nancystanislas.slogan: A king's gift to Nancy, fenced in gold leaf.
nancystanislas.line: Built between 1752 and 1756 by architect Emmanuel Héré, its gilded gates by Jean Lamour earned Nancy the name 'City with Golden Gates'.

lunevillechateau.name: Château de Lunéville
lunevillechateau.slogan: Lorraine's own Versailles, with a courtyard made for strolling.
lunevillechateau.line: A fire on the night of 2 to 3 January 2003 destroyed much of its roof and collapsed the royal chapel's vault; restoration continues.

domremyhouse.name: Joan of Arc's House, Domrémy
domremyhouse.slogan: A stone cottage where a farm girl first heard the voices.
domremyhouse.line: In 1429, at Joan's request, Charles VII exempted Domrémy and Greux from taxes 'forever'; the Revolution ended that.

nancyvillamajorelle.name: Villa Majorelle
nancyvillamajorelle.slogan: Curves, ironwork and stained glass, all in a cabinetmaker's home.
nancyvillamajorelle.line: Henri Sauvage designed it at about 24, in 1901-1902, as his first project, for furniture maker Louis Majorelle.

baccaratcristalmuseum.name: Baccarat Crystal Museum
baccaratcristalmuseum.slogan: Chandeliers that have lit palaces, glowing in a Lorraine town.
baccaratcristalmuseum.line: Louis XV authorised the Baccarat glassworks in 1764, at the request of the Bishop of Metz.
